## Unowned PR batch — branch disposition execution, 2026-11-07

Drew's ruling (2026-11-07 21:53 CST): on the laptop, uncommitted or ahead branches get committed and pushed, then clean local branches fully in origin get deleted; in origin, behind-only branches and merged-PR heads get deleted; branches ahead with real changes (not just merge commits) get a PR each. This issue owns the resulting unowned PR batch.

Triage: ONE triage task per repo on its pilot queue (repo-health-code-pilot / repo-health-opencode-pilot / repo-health-openchamber-pilot / repo-health-nix-pilot) covers that repo's list below. Per PR: validate the work is real and current; outcome is either close the PR with reason or route it to impl/finish/merge as a follow-on fix task. Triage annotates/validates/routes only — it never counts as done. Duplicate families named in the review must be resolved pairwise before either member is closed (code: queue/2956-173-blob-gate-wire PR #3917 vs queue/5874-173-blob-gate-shepherd; rescue/3275-1980-local-2026-11-01 vs queue/3275-1980-cli-run PR #2714. opencode: queue/2648-652-gitobj-timeout vs queue/2648-652-pack-timeout; queue/3041-631-subagent-ancestor vs rescue/3041-631-subagent-ancestor-2026-11-01; effect-patterns-triage vs queue/7181-1496-effect-patterns. openchamber: queue/10555-1652-project-knowledge-i18n vs -uk-i18n).

Evidence: execution log `~/workspace/scratch/branch-disposition-2026-11-07.md`; read-only review `~/workspace/scratch/branch-ahead-review-2026-11-07.md`. The 209-entry branch-cleanup registry is dispositioned under the same rules (207 resolved; the 2 backup/* entries kept under the preservation rule).

**This body is the header. The four per-repo lists are the first comments on this issue** (code list in 3 comments, then opencode, openchamber, darwin-nix).
